Go constrains the parameters to pointer types (`T *U`), so nil maps onto None exactly, and the function returns `a` itself when non-nil and `b` otherwise — pointer identity preserved on both branches. `a.or(b)` is the same, including the non-shortcutting property the Go doc comment warns about: `b` is an already-evaluated argument in both languages (Rust's shortcutting form is the separate `or_else`). rustc check: `Some(&1).or(Some(&2))` is `Some(1)`, `None.or(Some(&2))` is `Some(2)`, `None.or(None)` is `None` — all three Go branches reproduced, with no empty-versus-nil ambiguity because Option has exactly two states.

roster.owner: The vfstest.Clock interface (upstream/tsc/internal/vfs/vfstest/vfstest.go:37-40) requires SinceStart, but MapFS never calls it — the only clock read in the whole file is `m.clock.Now()`. The callers that DO call SinceStart supply their own Clock implementations and belong to later steps: upstream/tsc/internal/execute/tsctests/sys.go:187-189 (TestSys) and upstream/tsc/internal/execute/tsc/emit_test.go:73, :100, :120, consumed at upstream/tsc/internal/execute/tsc/emit.go:53 `result.times.totalTime = input.Sys.SinceStart()`.
